bullets.title: META: $50B+ Louisiana data center push; MS raises '27/'28 capex 29%/22%
bullets.body: Meta confirmed >$50B investment in Richland Parish, Louisiana targeting 5GW compute capacity with 1,000+ jobs, pushing total project cost to ~$250B. Morgan Stanley's Nowak raised META '27/'28 capex to $225B/$250B; META remains MS top pick with 5 under-appreciated call options including AI API monetization (~$2 of 2028 EPS per 100MW). META also exploring AI cloud services entry per Roth.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex raised to $1.4T by '28; AMZN/GOOGL both OW at MS
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Nowak raised five-hyperscaler capex aggregate to ~$1.2T in 2027 and ~$1.4T in 2028 (up ~10% vs prior), with total compute capacity reaching 120GW by 2028 vs 30GW in 2025. AMZN capex raised 15%/29% to $308B/$318B; GOOGL capex $350B/$375B. Cost per GW up ~20% on memory and powered-shell inflation; build timelines stretched to 3 years. Both AMZN and GOOGL rated OW with hyperscale revenues/profitability set to accelerate.

bullets.title: TSM: June revenue $13.8B, +68% YoY; Q2 record; 1.4nm on track
bullets.body: TSMC reported June revenue of ~$13.8B (+67.9% YoY, +6.2% MoM), driving record Q2 revenue of $39.63B (+36% YoY) on AI demand. Separately, TSMC's 1.4nm process is reportedly progressing without roadblocks with first fab nearing completion and pilot production expected Q3 2027. Klein notes management likely to raise FY26 guide from 'above 30%' to 'at least 35%' or higher at upcoming earnings.

bullets.title: NVDA/semis: SK Hynix ADR selloff pressures memory names; MS still optimistic on cycle
bullets.body: SK Hynix's record 15% single-day plunge in Korea (down 38% from ATH, KOSPI hit 7th circuit breaker of 2026) spilled into US premarket: MU -5.3%, SNDK -5.6%, WDC -5.1%. Morgan Stanley post-NVDA NDR remains 'optimistic about memory cycle duration, not peak earnings power.' Wolfe sees AVGO and NVDA trading at discount and recommends owning both; MU remains bullish at Wolfe despite post-earnings pullback due to customer SCAs providing multi-year visibility.

bullets.title: AVGO: Wolfe bullish; $5B FY27 datacenter guidance underappreciated by Street
bullets.body: Wolfe notes Street estimates miss the full $5B FY27 datacenter guidance for AVGO; management highly optimistic 20GW XPV financing vehicle gets done, leaving ~14GW incremental OpenAI/Anthropic capacity for FY28. AVGO successfully defended competitive moat against MediaTek and Google internal threats. Wolfe recommends owning both AVGO and NVDA to hedge individual company risk.

bullets.title: SHOP upgraded to Buy at Jefferies ($160 PT) on agentic commerce leadership
bullets.body: Jefferies upgrades SHOP to Buy with $160 PT, citing leadership in agentic commerce and pricing upside. SHOP also trading +2.8% in premarket on the Jefferies upgrade. Wolfe Bay Area bus tour separately flagged positive SHOP CoCo momentum.

bullets.title: AAPL: Citi raises PT to $365 from $315 (Buy); acquires SigScalr/SigLens assets
bullets.body: Citi raised its Apple price target to $365 from $315, maintaining Buy; stock hit a 52-week high (+51.2% YTD) at $321.30. Apple separately acquired SigScalr assets including SigLens (data log management/observability tool), disclosed to EU in March 2026; financial terms undisclosed. Hedgeye flagged AAPL short black book sessions ahead but no near-term rating action.

bullets.title: NFLX: Oppenheimer cuts PT to $100 (from $120) but reiterates Outperform on ad upside
bullets.body: Oppenheimer trimmed NFLX PT to $100 from $120 but kept Outperform, arguing current ~$6 CPM vs. peer $15 implies a $4B-$11.6B ad revenue opportunity. Proprietary survey shows 5x more respondents watching 'more' vs 'less'; 2H content slate has 104 releases vs 95 in 2H25. Incremental EBIT margins suggest 4% upside to LT estimates vs. Street. NFLX also cited as a potential bidder for Letterboxd per M&A summary.

bullets.title: DIS: Wells Fargo cuts PT to $125 (from $146), suggests exiting streaming; Benchmark initiates Buy at $115
bullets.body: Wells Fargo cut DIS PT to $125 from $146, arguing Disney would be better off exiting streaming (only 13% DTC OMs) and returning to production/licensing. Separately, Benchmark initiated DIS at Buy with $115 PT, citing IP monetization, Experiences as largest earnings contributor, and ESPN as the largest strategic opportunity.

bullets.title: WBD/PSKY: State antitrust lawsuit to block Paramount-WBD deal filed today
bullets.body: Around a dozen states led by California and New York AGs are expected to file an antitrust lawsuit today seeking to block Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, primarily over job-loss concerns. Paramount has offered concessions to California AG and is willing to divest its film distribution JV with Universal to address EU concerns. PSKY threatening to relocate out-of-state if deal is blocked.

bullets.title: MDB: GA's Search/Vector/Hybrid Search; Iceberg integration; KeyBanc positive
bullets.body: MongoDB GA'd Search, Vector Search, and Hybrid Search for Enterprise Advanced and Community Edition; launched Native Reranking preview; added Stream Processing writes to Apache Iceberg enabling near real-time sync. KeyBanc Data Dispatch noted MDB among the most positive meetings on the Wolfe Bay Area bus tour. MDB -3.6% on the week but data/analytics sector outperformed broader software on the week.

bullets.title: APP: Citi maintains Buy; Week 28 US ecommerce store growth solid at 1.3% WoW
bullets.body: AppLovin Ads eCommerce client count reached 10,471 (+2.4% WoW) as of July 10, with US store count at 4,946 (+1.3% WoW). Hong Kong losses moderating (share down only 50bps WoW vs 850bps monthly). Store growth decelerating from 3.1% in 1Q26 to 2.2% in 2Q26. Citi maintains Buy.

bullets.title: DDOG: Acquires Adaptive ML; ESTC cuts metrics pricing 75%; sector +1.1% WoW
bullets.body: Datadog acquired Adaptive ML (RLOps platform) to enhance domain-specific AI agents in Bits AI. ESTC cut metrics pricing 75% on TSDS-based Serverless, positioning ~30% cheaper than DDOG. DDOG +89.4% YTD; ESTC +3.8% on the week. DDOG also achieved GovRAMP High authorization for government use.

bullets.title: FISV: Options vol 308% above avg on rumors banks in early talks to buy Fiserv network
bullets.body: FISV saw 46.8K options contracts, 308% above its 30-day average, with a 10.66 put/call ratio (call-heavy) on rumors that banks are in early talks to acquire the Fiserv network. No confirmation of deal.

bullets.title: QCOM: Street missing full $5B FY27 datacenter guidance; remains show-me story
bullets.body: Wolfe notes Street estimates miss QCOM's full $5B FY27 datacenter revenue guidance; handset revenue expected to decline $5-6B YoY in FY27. QCOM remains a 'show-me story' on datacenter given far-out targets and inorganic FY27 revenue components.

bullets.title: INTC: Unveils space-grade 18A Starfire SoCs; $5.7B Ireland fab investment
bullets.body: Intel unveiled Starfire space-grade SoCs on its 18A process technology. Intel also announced a $5.7B capital investment in its Ireland fab complex for Xeon 6 and Intel 3 node chip production. UBS notes INTC beat-and-raise on server CPU strength with focus on 18A/14A foundry execution.

bullets.title: RBLX: Citi Buy maintained; 3Q26 CCU trends improving sequentially
bullets.body: Roblox Week 28 average peak CCUs of 17.3M (-5% YoY) are sequentially improving, with 3Q26 trends consistent with $1.88B bookings guidance. 2Q26 CCUs slightly below midpoint guidance at $1.57B bookings equivalent.

bullets.title: DKNG: Bernstein cuts FY26/27 estimates on customer-friendly Q2 sports outcomes
bullets.body: Bernstein lowered DKNG FY26 and FY27 estimates citing customer-friendly sports outcomes in Q2 and higher marketing spend. No rating change disclosed.

bullets.title: SNOW: Marketplace partners earned >$100M gross bookings (+277% YoY) in 6 months; Wolfe positive on CoCo
bullets.body: Snowflake Marketplace partners earned >$100M in gross bookings over the past 6 months (+277% YoY). Wolfe Bay Area bus tour notes SNOW confident in Cortex Catalog (CoCo) delivering a strong independent revenue stream with robust migration pipeline. SNOW Cortex Code evaluated as a general-purpose AI coding tool with <5% Snowflake-specific workloads.

bullets.title: MSFT: Exec Nick Parker departing for NVDA; CEO flags 'hard trust boundary' AI architecture
bullets.body: MSFT EVP Nick Parker is joining NVDA as EVP of Worldwide Field Operations per Truist. MSFT CEO Nadella argued enterprise AI requires a 'hard trust boundary' around data, favoring private/tenant-controlled architecture over single frontier-model coupling—a thesis aligned with Palantir's data sovereignty messaging.
